# GNU grep, GNU sed and findutils.

grep beta a.txt b.txt
grep -n -i BETA a.txt
grep -c a a.txt b.txt
grep -v a a.txt
grep -w the words
grep -o 'o[a-z]' words
grep -E 'qu|la' words
grep -F 'a.t' a.txt
grep -r one dir
grep -l beta a.txt b.txt empty
grep -L beta a.txt b.txt empty
grep -q gamma a.txt; echo $?
grep nothing a.txt; echo $?
grep beta missing; echo $?
grep -s beta missing; echo $?
grep '[' a.txt; echo $?
grep -A1 alpha a.txt
grep -B1 -n gamma a.txt
grep -C1 beta a.txt
grep -m1 a a.txt
grep -h beta a.txt b.txt
grep -e alpha -e gamma a.txt
grep -x beta a.txt
grep text bin
grep -a text bin
sed s/a/A/ a.txt
sed 's/a/A/g' a.txt
sed -n 2p a.txt
sed 2d a.txt
sed '$!N;s/\n/ /' a.txt
sed -n '/beta/,$p' a.txt b.txt
sed 'y/abc/xyz/' a.txt
sed -E 's/(a)(l)/\2\1/' a.txt
sed '1i\
first' a.txt
sed '2a appended' a.txt
sed = a.txt
sed -n l tabs
sed 's/x' a.txt
sed q5 a.txt; echo $?
sed -s 1d a.txt b.txt
cp a.txt e.txt && sed -i 's/beta/BETA/' e.txt && cat e.txt
find dir | sort
find dir -type f | sort
find dir -name 't*' | sort
find . -maxdepth 1 -type d | sort
find dir -empty
find dir -newer a.txt
find dir -name one -print -quit
find dir -path '*/sub/*' | sort
find dir -type f -exec echo found {} \; | sort
find dir -type f -exec echo {} + | tr ' ' '\n' | sort
find missing; echo $?
find dir -bogus; echo $?
find dir -size -1k -type f | sort
find dir -mindepth 2 | sort
find dir \( -name one -o -name two \) -print | sort
find dir ! -name '*o*' | sort
find dir -printf '%f %d %y\n' | sort
